html:
Razia Sultan ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1236 to 1240. She was the only woman ever to sit on the throne of Delhi as sultan.

She was the daughter of Iltutmish, who passed over his sons and named her his heir. After his death the nobles first crowned her brother, who proved useless, and then turned to her. She ruled in her own right. She held open court, rode at the head of her army and dropped the veil in public, which shocked many of the Turkish nobles.

Those nobles, a powerful clique of former slave officers, wanted a weak ruler. Her favour to Jamal ud-Din Yaqut, an African officer, gave them a reason to revolt. The governor of Bathinda, Altunia, rose against her and took her prisoner. She married him and the two marched on Delhi, but they were defeated and killed in 1240.

Her reign was short, but she is remembered as a capable ruler in the Mamluk dynasty who lost because she was a woman in a court of men.
sum: Razia Sultan ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1236 to 1240. She was the only woman ever to sit on the throne of Delhi as sultan.
